findings.title: Silent truncation: bodies larger than maxBody are returned as success
findings.evidence: body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxBody)) then return body, nil
findings.recommendation: Read one byte past the cap and fail explicitly when exceeded, e.g. io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxBody+1)) and return an error such as 'body exceeds %d bytes' when len(body) > maxBody; or document the truncation in the Get doc comment and return a truncation flag. Never return partial bytes with a nil error.

findings.title: nil *http.Client panics instead of returning an error
findings.recommendation: Guard at entry: if client == nil { client = http.DefaultClient } (or return a wrapped error), since Get is an exported API taking a pointer the caller controls.

findings.title: Body closed without being drained, so the connection is not reused
findings.evidence: defer resp.Body.Close() with no io.Copy(io.Discard, ...) drain on error paths
findings.recommendation: On the non-200 path (and after a limited read) drain a bounded amount into io.Discard before Close so the underlying keep-alive connection can be returned to the pool.

findings.title: New exported API ships with no tests, especially no oversize-body or timeout test
findings.evidence: func Get(ctx context.Context, client *http.Client, url string) ([]byte, error) {
findings.evidence_quote: func Get(ctx context.Context, client *http.Client, url string) ([]byte, error) {
findings.recommendation: Add table-driven tests using httptest.Server: 200 with normal body, body just over maxBody (assert an error, not silent truncation), non-200 status, and a handler that blocks past the timeout (assert context.DeadlineExceeded wraps through).
